title: Biggest Pool
statement: Wall heights stand in a row, one unit apart. Choose two walls; the water they hold is the distance between them times the shorter wall. Return the largest amount of water.

examples.explanation: Walls at index 1 and 8: width 7, height 7, water 49.

answerKey.pattern: Two pointers from both ends, moving the shorter wall inward
keyPoints: left = 0, right = last index; area = (right - left) * min(heights)
Move the pointer at the shorter wall inward: the shorter wall cannot do better with a narrower width
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Try every pair of walls: O(n^2)

hints: Trying every pair is O(n^2). Start with the widest pair: which wall limits it?
The shorter wall limits the water. Moving the taller one inward can only make things worse.
So move the pointer at the shorter wall and keep the best area seen.
